chapters.title: Teaching capability and field instruction
chapters.summary: Balloon aerial mapping and field GIS at Black Rock Forest in 2017 preceded the 2021 Provost-supported drone-teaching capability. Callicoon, Lamont, William Paterson, Hemlock Hill and educator workshops connect field observations, instrumentation and spatial analysis.

chapters.title: Community-engaged mapping
chapters.summary: SDEV4650 connects students, the Staten Island Urban Center and community partners around waterfront questions. The work extends from the 60 Hannah Street field session to later North Shore mapping and partner access to spatial information.

chapters.title: NYC Parks UAS research
chapters.summary: EFPL’s developing NYC Parks portfolio includes repeated Four Sparrow Marsh surveys, North Shore Esplanade and Morningside Park mapping, and forthcoming work at Highbridge Park. North Shore also continues the Staten Island community partnership.

chapters.title: HOT, UNZA and mapping in Zambia
chapters.summary: Work with the Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team and University of Zambia colleagues connects international exchange, field methods and selected-site mapping around Mtukuzi. Fieldwork also contributed to a learning module developed for TOPSTSCHOOL.

chapters.title: Current research and forthcoming work
chapters.summary: At Lamont, terrain and surface information support investigation of wind dynamics alongside field measurements. Ongoing Morningside research, methods development and forthcoming Highbridge work extend the program with partners.

case_studies.details: The 2021 Provost Emerging Technology Grant supported equipment for Drones and AR/VR for 3D Modeling in GIS. Earth Institute Course Support funded travel and accommodation. These were distinct forms of support.

case_studies.title: Black Rock Forest balloon mapping
case_studies.place: Black Rock Forest, Cornwall, New York
case_studies.summary: Three Columbia GIS courses combined low-cost balloon aerial mapping with GPS and mobile field observations at Black Rock Forest.
case_studies.question: How can students build aerial-mapping systems and connect their images with ground observations?
case_studies.contribution: Approximately 35 students worked with Public Lab balloon kits, true-color and modified infrared cameras, GPS and Collector for ArcGIS. Tree observations included hemlock woolly adelgid indicators and diameter measurements.
case_studies.credit: CIESIN · Columbia University · Kytt MacManus · Dara Mendeloff · Greg Yetman · Sara Lytle · Christina Paton · Gina Dinnegan · Fall 2017 GIS students
case_studies.details: A Fall 2017 Earth Institute Course Support Grant supported the field visit. Kytt MacManus, Dara Mendeloff and Greg Yetman instructed the courses, with teaching assistants Sara Lytle and Christina Paton; Gina Dinnegan helped organize the trip. At the Upper Reservoir the group used Mobius Action Cams with a 6 mm true-color lens and a modified infrared/NDVI camera. High winds limited the balloon operation, while usable source images and mobile field observations were produced. This earlier balloon-based work is a precursor within the teaching chapter.

case_studies.title: William Paterson tree mapping
case_studies.summary: A workshop hosted by Nicole Davi connected campus tree observations in ArcGIS Field Maps with drone-derived imagery and elevation products.
case_studies.question: How can field tree observations be interpreted alongside aerial imagery and reconstructed surface information?
case_studies.contribution: Field GIS, visible-light and thermal observations, and subsequent Drone2Map products provided complementary views of the campus. A public project web map retains the spatial products and tree-observation layer.
case_studies.credit: EFPL · Columbia University · William Paterson University · Kytt MacManus · Nicole Davi · participating students
case_studies.details: After the March 11 workshop, Kytt shared optical and thermal source imagery, Skydio 3D source imagery, processed products and workshop materials. The follow-up identified elevation products as potentially useful for tree identification. The current public map includes true orthomosaics, DSM/DTM and relief/contour layers, plus field tree observations. Those products do not establish census completeness, species-identification accuracy or calibrated thermal temperatures. Product displays use the published imagery alone on a neutral background.

case_studies.title: Hemlock Hill field instrumentation
case_studies.summary: SDEV3450 students worked with Watershed Agricultural Council partners on ground observations, positioning, photogrammetry and LiDAR field methods at an agricultural site.
case_studies.question: How do ground measurements, control observations and complementary aerial sensors fit together in a field-data workflow?
case_studies.contribution: The field exercise connected GNSS/GCP and total-station work with Mavic 3 photogrammetry, IF1200A LiDAR acquisition, a multispectral camera configuration, data offload and processing.
case_studies.credit: EFPL · Columbia University · SDEV3450 students · Watershed Agricultural Council · Amy Faulkner · Andy Cheung · Donald Arrant · Ryan Naatz
case_studies.details: The documented April 15 field session combined student and partner activity with complementary instruments. Existing processed photogrammetric outputs include orthomosaic, DSM, DTM, point cloud and mesh; these are distinct from the separately logged IF1200A LiDAR acquisition. Selected camera views retain the original sensor colors without treating them as calibrated NDVI. No agricultural outcome, independent checkpoint accuracy or complete farm inventory is claimed.
